sources.title: 2026 November General Election Absentee Report (September 28)
sources.text: JACKSON, Miss. - As of Monday, September 28, 2026, the Statewide Election Management System (SEMS) reported a total of 8,787 absentee ballots requested , 8,463 absentee ballots sent , and 4,148 absentee ballots received in the state of Mississippi for the 2026 November General Election on Tuesday, November 3 . As a reminder, the requested total reflects the number of Mississippi voters who have requested an absentee ballot through their local Circuit Clerk's Office. The sent total reflects the number of absentee ballots sent to voters from Circuit Clerk’s Offices. The received total reflects the number of completed absentee ballots returned to Circuit Clerk’s Offices. CLICK HERE TO VIEW THE ABSENTEE REPORT ADDITIONAL REMINDERS A sample ballot may be accessed on the Secretary of State’s Office website . Mississippians who have requested an absentee ballot may track their ballot utilizing the My Election Day portal . The in-person absentee voting deadline for the 2026 November General Election is Saturday, October 31 . All mail-in absentee ballots must be postmarked by Election Day (November 3) . The Resolution Board can begin processing absentee ballots at the opening of the polls on Election Day (7 a.m.). County election officials can tabulate ballots at the closing of the polls on Election Day (7 p.m.). For questions regarding absentee voting, please contact our Elections Division at ElectionsAnswers@sos.ms.gov , call the Elections Hotline at 1-800-829-6786, or visit YallVote.ms .

sources.title: Upcoming Voter Registration Deadline for the 2026 November General Election
sources.text: JACKSON, Miss. - Applicants who register in-person in the Circuit Clerk’s Office and those who mail registration applications postmarked no later than Monday, October 5, are eligible to vote in the 2026 General Election on Tuesday, November 3 . Mississippians may utilize YallVote.ms to download a mail-in voter registration application , verify voter registration status , or update voter registration information . For those who are already registered to vote, in-person and mail-in absentee ballots are now available in Circuit Clerk’s Offices. To learn more about the updated procedure for in-person absentee voting, click here . To access the full 2026 Elections Calendar , visit the Secretary of State's website or click here . The Secretary of State's Office is your primary and trusted source for election information. For questions, please contact the Elections Division at 1-800-829-6786, email ElectionsAnswers@sos.ms.gov , or visit YallVote.ms . Important Dates for the 2026 General Election Monday, October 5 - Voter Registration Deadline for the 2026 General Election Saturday, October 24 - Saturday In-Person Absentee Voting Begins Saturday, October 31 - In-Person Absentee Voting Deadline Tuesday, November 3 - General Election Day Deadline for the postmark of mail-in absentee ballots

supported_article.headline: Mississippi voter registration deadline is Oct. 5; absentee voting underway
supported_article.excerpt: Mississippi voter registration closes October 5. Absentee ballots are already available, with Saturday service beginning October 24.
supported_article.body:
Mississippi voters have until Monday, October 5, to register for the November 3, 2026, General Election, according to a September 28 announcement from the Mississippi Secretary of State’s Office. Applicants may register in person at their local Circuit Clerk’s Office or mail an application postmarked no later than October 5.

For voters who are already registered, in-person and mail-in absentee ballots are available at Circuit Clerk’s Offices. Saturday in-person absentee voting begins October 24. The deadline for voting absentee in person is Saturday, October 31. The October 24 date applies to Saturday availability, rather than the start of all in-person absentee voting.

A separate September 28 report from the Secretary of State listed 8,787 absentee ballots requested statewide for the November election. The Statewide Election Management System also recorded 8,463 ballots sent to voters and 4,148 completed absentee ballots returned to Circuit Clerk’s Offices.

The requested total counts voters who asked their local Circuit Clerk’s Office for an absentee ballot. The sent total counts ballots sent to voters, while the received total counts completed ballots returned to those offices. These figures describe statewide activity as of September 28.

Voters who have requested an absentee ballot may track it through the My Election Day portal. Mail-in absentee ballots must be postmarked by Election Day, November 3. Resolution Boards can begin processing absentee ballots when polls open at 7 a.m.; county election officials can tabulate ballots when polls close at 7 p.m.

YallVote.ms provides access to a mail-in registration application, registration-status checks, registration updates and the full election calendar. A sample ballot is also available on the Secretary of State’s website. For questions, contact the Elections Division at 1-800-829-6786 or ElectionsAnswers@sos.ms.gov.

unsupported_article.headline: Mississippi voters face Oct. 5 registration deadline ahead of Nov. 3 election
unsupported_article.body:
Mississippi voters who are not registered must complete registration by Monday, Oct. 5, to be eligible to vote in the 2026 November General Election on Tuesday, Nov. 3, according to the Mississippi Secretary of State’s Office. In-person applicants must register through their Circuit Clerk’s Office, while mailed applications must be postmarked no later than Oct. 5.

Voters can use YallVote.ms to download a mail-in voter registration application, check their registration status or update registration information. The Secretary of State’s Office said in-person and mail-in absentee ballots are available through Circuit Clerk’s Offices for voters who are already registered.

Absentee voting deadlines

In-person absentee voting begins Saturday, Oct. 24, and ends Saturday, Oct. 31. Mail-in absentee ballots must be postmarked by Election Day, Nov. 3, according to the Secretary of State’s election information.

As of Monday, Sept. 28, the Statewide Election Management System reported 8,787 absentee ballots requested, 8,463 sent and 4,148 received statewide for the November election. The Secretary of State’s Office said the requested figure counts voters who requested ballots through their local Circuit Clerk’s Office, the sent figure counts ballots sent to voters, and the received figure counts completed ballots returned to Circuit Clerk’s Offices.

Absentee ballots can begin being processed at 7 a.m. on Election Day, while county election officials can tabulate ballots when polls close at 7 p.m., the Secretary of State’s Office reported. Voters who requested an absentee ballot may track it through the My Election Day portal.

Questions about registration or absentee voting can be directed to the Elections Division at 1-800-829-6786 or ElectionsAnswers@sos.ms.gov. The Secretary of State’s Office also directs voters to YallVote.ms for election information and registration resources.
